n.story:
In the coming years, your role will shift from high-volume manual labor to quality assurance and specialized garment care. As computer vision and robotic sorters take over the repetitive tasks of identifying fabrics, reading care labels, and sorting items, the 'bulk' of the work week disappears. You will no longer spend hours squinting at tiny tags or manually separating cottons from synthetics; instead, you will oversee a fleet of automated systems that handle the standard items, intervening only when the AI flags a delicate accessory or a complex garment that requires a human touch.

Your expertise will be redirected toward high-value customer service and 'edge-case' problem solving. When a machine cannot determine the best way to treat a vintage silk or a multi-material designer piece, you are the expert who makes the call. You will use AI-powered tools to analyze fabric health and stain types, providing a level of precision in garment restoration that was previously impossible. You are evolving from a manual laborer into a textile care technician.
